title: Three-dimensional generalized-Maxwell harmonic bar
purpose: Verify direct frequency-domain lowering of independent complex bulk and shear moduli, harmonic traction, inertia, phasor results and cycle-energy closure on a real PETSc build.

execution.command: python -m pytest -q tests/test_viscoelasticity.py -k harmonic && agentfem mpi-run -n 2 -- python -m pytest -q tests/test_parallel_viscoelasticity.py
execution.evidence: A homogeneous bar first checks quasi-static complex compliance and independent bulk/shear relaxation. A second fixed--traction bar includes inertia and is compared over three meshes with the closed-form one-dimensional complex wave solution derived from the published generalized viscoelastic rod boundary-value problem. The quasi-static bar is also solved on two MPI ranks; its phasor, energy ledger and four-field collective XDMF/ParaView output are required to remain rank-consistent.

observables: Real and imaginary end-displacement phasor components.
Complex bulk, shear, Young and Poisson quantities at the solve frequency.
Cycle-mean stored and kinetic energy, external input and material dissipation per cycle, their balance error, and mean dissipated power.
Linear solver convergence reason and iterations plus the independently assembled global, real-block and imaginary-block A*x-b residuals.
acceptance: The assembled end displacement must match the analytical complex compliance to the declared numerical tolerance.
Independent bulk and shear relaxation ratios must recover the analytical complex axial and lateral displacement phasors.
The inertial end displacement error must decrease over 4, 8 and 16 longitudinal cells and finish below 0.2 percent.
External input over one cycle must close against viscoelastic material loss to the declared tolerance.
The independently assembled A*x-b residual must close globally and in both real phasor blocks rather than relying only on the preconditioned KSP norm.
The result must expose U_REAL, U_IMAG, U_AMPLITUDE and U_PHASE without requiring a complex PETSc installation.
A two-rank solve must reproduce the analytical compliance, identical global energy evidence on every rank, and one collective ParaView dataset containing all four phasor fields.
A passive generalized-Maxwell material must report nonnegative loss moduli and positive dissipation at positive frequency.
Frequency, angular frequency and the exp(+i*omega*t) convention must remain explicit in the result evidence.

quantities.name: normalized_complex_end_displacement
quantities.description: End displacement divided by traction times length over the instantaneous Young modulus for one branch with ratio 0.4 and omega*tau=1.

quantities.name: inertial_tip_relative_error
quantities.description: Relative error of the finest fixed--traction inertial-bar end phasor against the closed-form one-dimensional wave solution.

quantities.name: relative_cycle_energy_balance_error
quantities.description: External cycle input minus material loss, normalized by the declared harmonic energy scale.

limitations: This is an automated analytical verification derived from a published boundary-value problem, not an independent external finite-element result curve.
The current harmonic provider accepts one isotropic 3D material, homogeneous strong constraints and one common load phase.
Near-incompressible mixed formulations, near-resonance preconditioning, automated frequency sweeps, multiple materials, MPC/weak constraints and complex modes remain promotion gates.
